minutes.headline: Committee decided any new town building houses only town offices — no school departments — after prior project's scope crept
minutes.summary: The Building Design Committee reviewed the TC Pacios walkthrough (records storage volume, roof condition) and worked through detailed space-needs planning for a town hall annex — conference rooms, counter space, storage and records-retention rules — using an AI-generated planning guide and employee questionnaire results. The group agreed to bring several options to the select board rather than to town meeting directly, to keep the project limited to town administration only, and to seek a small architectural scoping effort before committing to full design, explicitly to avoid the scope creep and cost overruns of the town's earlier failed combined town/school project.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of the July 28th joint meeting with the select board.
Approve the minutes of the August 3rd, 2026 meeting.

budget_items.what_was_said: A member recalled the town manager mentioning capital money had been allocated for digitizing records stored at TC Pacios, but nobody present could recall the amount or confirm it had been spent.
A prior 2025 study put renovating Town Hall at roughly one figure and renovating the Ritter building at roughly another; a member said combining the two would have been an affordable, doable project.
A member recalled that adding PACK space in the basement of the earlier failed project alone was described as costing over a stated figure, illustrating scope creep.

budget_items.topic: Failed prior town hall/school project design cost
budget_items.what_was_said: A member noted the committee spent a stated sum on design work for the earlier combined town/school project, which itself was priced at a stated total, without doing this level of requirements discussion first.
A member suggested a November town meeting might be asked for a modest sum to fund early architectural scoping support rather than a full design contract.
A member contrasted the small scoping effort being proposed with a full design effort, which he said was not what they were asking for at this stage.

decisions.decision: The committee will present the select board with several space-planning options rather than bringing multiple choices directly to town meeting, leaving the select board to choose which option to advance.
Any new or renovated town facility will house only town administration functions, not school department offices, reversing the scope of the earlier failed project.

Pursue a smaller architectural/consultant scoping effort (layouts, square footage, utilities) before committing to a full design contract, rather than repeating the prior process of handing the project to an architect with no detailed requirements.
Ask department heads (assessor, town clerk, accounting, treasurer, payroll, town manager) to report their weekly meeting hours to help size conference room needs.

Determine, department by department, which records must legally be retained in paper and for how long, to size future storage needs rather than planning storage for records that could be digitized or discarded.
Next meeting set for August 31st; Steve Walton, the town's land use director, will be invited to join to discuss possibilities for the TC Pacios building.

what_happened.line: The committee decided any new or renovated town building will house only town administration, not school departments, reversing the scope of an earlier failed combined project.
The committee will bring the select board several space-planning options rather than taking multiple choices straight to town meeting.
Before committing to full design, the committee agreed to pursue a smaller architectural scoping effort covering layouts, square footage and utilities.
Department heads were asked to report weekly meeting hours and which records must legally stay on paper, to size conference rooms and storage for a future building.

why_it_matters: Limiting a future town building to town offices only means any school-department space needs would have to be addressed through a separate project, not this one.
Routing options through the select board rather than directly to town meeting shapes which choice residents eventually get to vote on and when.
An architectural scoping study, if funded, would likely appear as a town meeting warrant item before any full design contract is sought.

A possible November town meeting request for funding an early architectural scoping effort.
